name: Bladefist Bay
summary: Bladefist Bay opens onto the Great Sea along eastern Durotar, just beyond Orgrimmar's gates. Craggy bluffs rise above its shore, with Azshara's southern coast across the water.

sections.title: A Bay on the Great Sea
sections.body: Bladefist Bay meets the Great Sea along Durotar's northeastern edge. Rocky cliffs rise above its treacherous surf, just east of Orgrimmar, the Horde capital. Across the water to the north, Azshara's ancient red cliffs and ruins mark the far shore. The bay forms a boundary between Durotar and the open sea.

sections.title: Shadow of the Shattered Hand
sections.body: Kargath Bladefist gave the bay its name. Chieftain of the Shattered Hand clan, he severed his own hand and replaced it with a blade during the old Horde's trials on Draenor. Skull Rock lies nearby, where cultists and hidden rogue networks work in the shadows. The coast recalls the fierce, ruthless legacy of the clan's chieftain.

faq.q: Who is Bladefist Bay named after?
faq.answer: Bladefist Bay is named for Kargath Bladefist, chieftain of the Shattered Hand clan. He was known for replacing his severed hand with a lethal scythe blade.

aliases: how to get to bladefist bay
faq.answer: Bladefist Bay runs along Durotar's northeastern coast, east of Orgrimmar's main gates and south of Azshara across the water.

faq.q: What threats lurk around Bladefist Bay?
faq.answer: Skull Rock lies beside the shoreline, and its caverns harbor warlocks, demons, and members of the Burning Blade cult.

faq.q: Why is the bay sometimes called a midden heap?
faq.answer: No account from this era calls the bay a midden heap. It is a rocky stretch of Durotar's coast east of Orgrimmar, facing Azshara across the water.

angles.text: As an orc, you know the bay bears Kargath Bladefist's proud and brutal name, recalling the Shattered Hand clan's trials on Draenor.
As a rogue, you know the Shattered Hand operates in Orgrimmar's shadows as the Horde's guild of thieves and assassins. This coast carries a quiet resonance for covert operatives.
